title: Kuikúro language - Wikipedia
text: Kuikúro, also known as Amonap, Upper Xingu Cariban and Apalakiri, is a Cariban language spoken by the Kuikuro and Kalapalo peoples of Brazil. It is spoken in seven villages along the Culuene River in the Xingu Indigenous Park of Mato Grosso. title: Kalapalo - Wikipedia
text: The Kalapalo are an Indigenous people of Brazil. They are one of seventeen tribal groups who inhabit the Xingu National Park in the Upper Xingu River region of the state of Mato Grosso. They speak the Amonap language, a Cariban language, and one of four spoken languages in the area. They have a population of 569 as of 2010.

title: (PDF) Uvular taps in Kuikuro and Kalapalo - Academia.edu
text: Abstract This paper describe a sound that has not been included yet in the international Phonetic Alphabet. This sound is a uvular tap found in kuikuro and Kalapalo, two Upper-Xingu Carib languages from Brasil. Evidence for the existence of this sound which is a phoneme in Kuikuro and Kalapalo is based on acoustic and articulatory data.
